title: Impact of chronic coffee consumption on critical illness during intensive care treatment
summary: This work is intended as a prospective observational study to examine the initial course of critically ill  patients in connection with the amount of previous chronic coffee consumption. In particular, it is to be investigated whether the anamnestically coffee-consuming patients differ from coffee-naive patients with regard to intestinal function, hemodynamics and immunological parameters during the first days of treatment in critical illness.

interventions.name: Patients with chronic coffee consumption are examined in the first four days of critical illness with organ failure with regard to intestinal function and hemodynamics.
Patients without chronic coffee consumption are examined in the first four days of critical illness with organ failure with regard to intestinal function and hemodynamics.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Admission to the ICU within the last 12 hours
Existing critical illness, defined by the presence of at least one of the following parameters of organ failure:
AKIN II
Norepinephrine> 0.05 µg / kg body weight / min
GCS <12 without sedation
paO2 / FiO2 <300
SOFA> 10
qSOFA> 1
Exclusion criteria:
• Pregnant / breastfeeding patients
• Palliative treatment goal
• Known bowel dysfunction
